info.title: distribute.you API
info.description:
API Gateway for distribute.you.

## Quick Start

This document is large (every operation your key may call). Read it in pieces instead:

- `?view=onboarding`: open a first client, the same steps in the same order as the dashboard's sign-up flow, each with
  the route to call, what to send and what to keep (about 6k tokens).
- `?view=index`: every operation on one line, grouped by topic (about 13k tokens).
- `?tag=<topic>` (`&page=<n>` when the index says the topic has pages): the full detail of one topic.
- `?operation=<operationId>` (comma-separate several): the full detail of those operations only.

Each works on `GET /v1/me/openapi.json` (your key's document) and `GET /openapi.json` (no key needed).

**Get a key.** Already have one (from the distribute.you dashboard, or `POST /v1/api-keys`)? Use it. An AI agent with no
account: `POST /v1/agent-signups/start` with `{email, phone}`, read the 6-digit code in that inbox, then
`POST /v1/agent-signups/complete` with `{email, code}`: the answer carries `apiKey`. No human needed.
Send the key as `Authorization: Bearer distrib.usr_...` on every call, nothing else.

**How to decide each step** (what to ask your user, what a good offer or audience looks like): read the skills our own
Copilot follows, `GET /v1/skills` then `GET /v1/skills/{slug}`.

Accounts opened through `/v1/agent-signups` have no free credit: free calls work at once; a call that spends money
answers `402 payment_required` until the prepay is paid (minimum $10, plus a required auto top-up: at least $15
whenever the balance falls below at least $5).

**`GET /v1/me`** says which user the key acts as and lists every organization
the key can act in (by name), each with its brands. A key belongs to its USER, not to one
organization: membership is checked on every request, so leaving an organization removes it
from the key. A key never carries staff, admin or beta powers. The dashboard is at
https://dashboard.distribute.you.

**Each request acts in ONE organization.** Name a brand (`?brandId=<id>`, the `x-brand-id`
header, or `brandId` in a JSON body; brand routes like `/v1/brands/{id}` name it in the path),
which selects the organization holding it, or name the organization (`?orgId=<id>` or the
`x-org-id` header). If you belong to exactly one organization you need to name nothing. If you
belong to several and name nothing, the request is refused with `400 org_target_required` and
the list of your organizations; no organization is ever picked by default.

## Storing provider keys (BYOK)

To store your own provider API keys (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic) for use in workflows:

```
POST /v1/keys
Authorization: Bearer distrib.usr_abc123...

{ "provider": "openai", "apiKey": "sk-..." }
```

## Error codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 401 | Missing or invalid Bearer token. The body's `code` says which: `missing_credentials`, `wrong_header` (key sent in a header other than `Authorization`), `invalid_admin_key`, `malformed_key`, `key_not_recognized` (mistyped OR revoked: revoked keys are erased, so the two cannot be told apart); `fix` says what to do |
| 503 | `key_validation_unavailable`: the key could not be checked right now; retry, do not replace the key |
| 400 | `org_target_required`: you belong to several organizations and the request named none (`organizations` lists them); `brand_in_several_orgs`: the brand is held by several of your organizations, add `orgId`; `brands_span_orgs`: the named brands are not in one organization |
| 403 | `org_not_member`: the named organization is not one of yours; `no_organization`: the key's user belongs to no organization |
| 404 | `brand_not_found`: none of your organizations holds that brand |
| 503 | `membership_unavailable`: your organizations could not be checked right now; retry |
| 402 | `payment_required` (accounts opened through `/v1/agent-signups`): the call costs money and the balance cannot cover it. `prepay` gives the route, minimums and an example body; `upstream` is the refusing service's own answer |
| 429 | Rate limit exceeded — see below |
| 502 | Identity resolution failed (internal service unreachable) |

## Rate limits

Every response carries your current rate-limit state, so you never have to guess
how fast you may go:

```
RateLimit: limit=600, remaining=597, reset=42
RateLimit-Policy: "authenticated";q=600;w=60, "anonymous";q=120;w=60
RateLimit-Limit: 600
RateLimit-Remaining: 597
RateLimit-Reset: 42
```

`reset` is **seconds until the current window rolls over**, not a timestamp.

| Policy | Applies to | Budget |
|--------|-----------|--------|
| `authenticated` | One API key (`Authorization: Bearer distrib.*`) | 600 requests / 60s |
| `anonymous` | One client IP, for endpoints that need no key | 120 requests / 60s |

Exceeding a budget returns **429** with a `Retry-After` header in seconds. Wait
that long and retry — the window is fixed, so a single wait clears it. Requests
made while throttled still count, so back off rather than polling the 429.

## Deprecation policy

Nothing in this document is deprecated today. To set what a campaign may
spend, use its sales funnel caps:
`PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps`
(the old per-campaign daily-budget operations are gone).

When something is deprecated, you learn it mechanically, from the API itself,
and with at least
**180 days** of notice:

- The operation is marked `deprecated: true` in this document.
- Every response it returns carries `Deprecation: @<unix-seconds>` (RFC 9745)
  and `Sunset: <HTTP-date>` (RFC 8594). `Sunset` is the earliest date the
  operation may stop working — never sooner than 180 days
  after `Deprecation`.
- A `Link: <url>; rel="deprecation"` header points at the replacement
  operation or the changelog entry.
- A deprecated operation keeps working until its sunset date. Deprecation is an
  announcement, not a removal.
- Removal happens only behind a new URL version prefix. `/v1` never changes
  meaning underneath a caller: a breaking change ships as `/v2`.

The same policy is machine-readable at the root of this document under
`x-deprecation-policy`.

bearerAuth.description:
Bearer token authentication.

Use an API key (`distrib.usr_*`) as your Bearer token. Create one via `POST /v1/api-keys` or in the dashboard.

Your key carries your org and user identity. No extra headers needed.

amountCents.description: The campaign's max budget for the period, in cents (decimal string, as billing-service sends it)

consumedCents.description: Spent so far in the period, in cents; null when it could not be measured

SalesFunnelCap.description: On a 402 with `reason`: the cap billing-service applied, verbatim

reason.description: On a 402 only: present when the spend was refused because the campaign (sales funnel) reached its MAX BUDGET (`sales_funnel_max_budget_reached`) or its max budget could not be read (`sales_funnel_max_budget_unreadable`). Adding credit does not help: raise the campaign's max budget. Absent on a plain insufficient-balance refusal.

message.description: Plain-words explanation, when the error carries one

summary.description: Plain sentences: which user, every organization the access reaches (by name, with its brands), and which organization this request acts in, or that each request must name one

user.description: null when the lookup failed (see lookupErrors)

organizations.description: Every organization this access can act in, each with its brands. For a staff user's key: every organization that holds a brand. null = lookup failed (see lookupErrors)

organization.description: The organization THIS request acts in. null when the request named none and the user belongs to several organizations, or when the lookup failed

brands.description: The brands of `organization`. [] = no brand yet; null = no organization targeted, or lookup failed

keyScope.description: For a user API key: what the key covers (its user, across that user's organizations; how to name the organization of a request; never staff/admin/beta powers). null for dashboard sessions

lookupErrors.description: Lookups that failed, with the upstream message. Empty when everything resolved

error.description: Short error, unchanged from earlier versions (e.g. "Invalid API key")

code.description: Why the request was refused before reaching a service. The `org_*` / `brand_*` / `no_organization` / `membership_unavailable` codes are about WHICH organization a user-key request acts in: name a brand (`brandId`) or an organization (`orgId`); `organizations` lists the choices when relevant. The other codes say why authentication failed. `wrong_header` = a user key was sent in a header other than `Authorization`. `key_not_recognized` covers both a mistyped key and a revoked one: revoked keys are erased, so the two cannot be told apart. `key_validation_unavailable` (HTTP 503) means the key could not be checked and says nothing about its validity.

organizations.description: For organization-target refusals: the organizations the caller can name with `orgId`

workflowSlug.description: Exact versioned workflow slug used for execution

workflowDynastySlug.description: Stable dynasty slug for the workflow lineage (unversioned)

featureDynastySlug.description: Stable dynasty slug for the feature lineage (unversioned)

featureInputs.description: Free-form JSONB inputs for the feature

status.description: Campaign status (e.g. 'active', 'stopped')

nextRunAt.description: Scheduled next run time for a gate-blocked campaign

workflowSlug.description: Exact versioned workflow slug (e.g. 'sales-email-cold-outreach-sienna-v3'). Use for pinning to a specific version. Provide this OR workflowDynastySlug.

workflowDynastySlug.description: Stable dynasty slug for the workflow lineage (e.g. 'sales-email-cold-outreach-sienna'). Campaign-service resolves to the latest version automatically. Preferred over workflowSlug for dashboard use.

brandUrls.description: Brand website URLs. First URL is the primary brand; additional URLs are secondary brands. Provide this (website path) OR brandIds (no-website path) — exactly one.

brandIds.description: Brand UUIDs of already-created brands (no-website path). First id is the primary brand. When provided, api-service skips the brandUrls→brand upsert and forwards these ids straight to campaign-service. Provide this OR brandUrls — exactly one.

featureSlug.description: Exact versioned feature slug. Use for pinning to a specific version. Provide this OR featureDynastySlug.

featureDynastySlug.description: Stable dynasty slug for the feature lineage (e.g. 'pr-cold-email-outreach'). Campaign-service resolves to the latest version automatically. Preferred over featureSlug for dashboard use.

featureInputs.description: Opaque feature inputs. Validated by key-presence against features-service, never inspected by api-service.

maxLeads.description: Maximum number of leads to contact

goal.description: Campaign's own optimization goal. Vocabulary owned by campaign-service — not enumerated here.

brandId.description: The brand whose funded pair is being started.

offerId.description: The offer whose money funds this pair. Absent is the pre-offer population.

featureSlug.description: The acquisition channel, as a features-service feature slug.

legKey.description: The leg the campaign is bought for, as published on features-service's channel catalogue. Stated together with offerId. Vocabulary owned downstream — not enumerated here.

leadId.description: The lead the reporting service named on the occurrence. Null on an event you push with `person`: that person is filed as a lead of each campaign that runs, read them in `ranLeads`.

recordedVia.description: Who recorded it, e.g. `trigger_events` for a push through this route.

status.description: `pending` (due later, or held a few minutes while the person is filed) | `firing` | `done`.

outcome.description: `ran` (at least one campaign ran) | `skipped` (see `skipReason`) | `failed` (every run failed); null until `status` is `done`.

skipReason.description: Why nothing ran, one reason: a campaign's own (e.g. `unfunded`, `run_in_flight`, `person_suppressed`), else `campaign_off`, `no_campaign`, `no_leg`; `run_failed` when `outcome` is `failed`. Null when it ran.

ranCampaignIds.description: The campaigns that ran for it (empty unless `outcome` is `ran`).

ranLeads.description: Per campaign that ran: the lead the event's person was filed as on that campaign. Empty when no run carried a lead.

processedAt.description: ISO date-time the outcome was written; null until done.

detail.description: Every per-campaign answer: `{legKeys, triggered[], skipped[], offCampaignIds}`, plus the `person` and `item` you sent.

replayed.description: `true` when `idempotencyKey` named an event already recorded (answered 200).

triggerId.description: A declared trigger id (GET /v1/public/channels `triggers[].id`), e.g. `email_pushed_via_api` to have an email you wrote sent. Unknown = 400 `unknown_trigger`.

brandId.description: Your brand (GET /v1/brands). Not one of your organization's brands = 404 `brand_not_in_org`.

offerId.description: The brand's offer the occurrence is about.

email.description: The person's email. Optional when `phone` is given in E.164 form: one of the two is required (neither = 400 naming `person.email`, nothing recorded).

phone.description: The person's phone number in E.164 form (`+` and country code, e.g. `+33612345678`; spaces and dashes are dropped). With no `email`, the phone alone identifies the person (e.g. someone who only gave their WhatsApp number): send `person: {phone, name?}`. It is also used to infer the person's timezone when you state none.

timezone.description: The person's IANA timezone name (e.g. `Europe/London`, `America/New_York`, `UTC`), so every message lands in their business hours. An offset such as `GMT+1` or `+01:00` is refused (400 naming `person.timezone`, nothing recorded). Absent = inferred from what we hold, notably the phone (a +44 number = Europe/London) or the email. A stated timezone always wins over an inferred one.

person.description: Who the occurrence is about, by identity: `email`, or an E.164 `phone` when you have no email (one of the two is required). Each campaign the trigger reaches files them as a lead of the brand and runs for them.

item.description: What the occurrence carries, any JSON (at most 20,000 characters), handed verbatim to the workflow that runs. For `email_pushed_via_api`: the email you wrote, `{subject, bodyHtml?, bodyText?}` (at least one body), sent as written.

example.subject: Hiring in Leeds?
example.bodyText:
Hi Sam,
I saw you are hiring...

idempotencyKey.description: Unique per organization: a retry returns the first event (`replayed: true`), recorded once.

occurredAt.description: When it happened (ISO date-time). Absent = now.

dueAt.description: When it must fire (ISO date-time). Later than now = recorded `pending` and fired then.

status.description: Run status (e.g. completed, failed)

startedAt.description: ISO timestamp when the run started

completedAt.description: ISO timestamp when the run completed

ownCostInUsdCents.description: Sum of this run's own costs (excludes descendants)

ownActualCostInUsdCents.description: Sum of this run's own costs with status='actual'

ownProvisionedCostInUsdCents.description: Sum of this run's own costs with status='provisioned'

positiveReplies.description: Positive replies (email-gateway recipientStats.repliesPositive). 0 is shown as 0.

deliveryRate.description: delivered/sent as a 0..1 ratio, served by email-gateway (recipientStats.deliveryRate). null when nothing was sent, or when email-gateway could not be reached (see unavailable)

costInUsdCents.description: Same value as the response's totalCostInUsdCents

notServed.description: Figures no producer serves yet, each naming the service that would serve it

unavailable.description: Producers that could not be reached for this response; their figures are null, not zero

contacted.description: Leads submitted to email provider (COUNT DISTINCT by lead)

sent.description: Recipients with at least one sent email

Needed only when the user belongs to several organizations and the request names no brand; otherwise optional.

XBrandId.description: Brand ID(s), comma-separated UUIDs. Supports multi-brand campaigns. Forwarded to downstream services. With a user key it also selects the organization the request acts in: the one of the user's organizations holding every named brand (same for `brandId` in the query or a JSON body).

RateLimit.description: Current rate-limit state for this caller, e.g. `limit=600, remaining=597, reset=42`. `reset` is seconds until the window rolls over.

RateLimit-Policy.description: Every budget this API applies, e.g. `"authenticated";q=600;w=60, "anonymous";q=120;w=60` — `q` is requests per window, `w` is the window in seconds.

RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests allowed in the current window.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests still available in the current window.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until the current window resets.

x-request-id.description: Correlation id — the `x-request-id` you sent, or one generated by the gateway.

Deprecation.description: Present ONLY on a deprecated operation. `@<unix-seconds>` (RFC 9745) — when the operation was announced as deprecated. Absent means the operation is not deprecated.

Sunset.description: Present ONLY on a deprecated operation. HTTP-date (RFC 8594) — the earliest date the operation may stop working, never less than 180 days after `Deprecation`.

Link.description: Present ONLY on a deprecated operation. `<url>; rel="deprecation"` — the replacement operation or the changelog entry.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded. Wait `Retry-After` seconds and retry; the budget that was exceeded is named in the body and described in `RateLimit-Policy`.

post.summary: Create a campaign
post.description:
Create a new campaign. Requires feature inputs and at least one of featureSlug/featureDynastySlug plus one of workflowSlug/workflowDynastySlug.

Use `workflowDynastySlug`/`featureDynastySlug` (preferred) to let campaign-service resolve to the latest version automatically. Use `workflowSlug`/`featureSlug` only to pin to a specific version. Feature inputs are validated by key-presence against features-service (api-service never inspects values).

The body is a PASSTHROUGH: the fields below are the ones the gateway itself needs, and every other field campaign-service accepts is forwarded unchanged. A sales-outreach campaign states what it sells as `offerId` plus the leg it is bought for as `legKey` — that is what the campaign is paced and priced on. The gateway neither infers nor defaults either: campaign-service's own 400 comes back verbatim.

A campaign does not pick who its pipes find or contact: each pipe's lead strategy decides that. Browse and extend the strategies with the lead-strategy catalogue (`/v1/tactics`, `/v1/strategies`, `/v1/plays`).

post.summary: Start the campaign for a funded pair
post.description:
Start the campaign for a (sales funnel x acquisition channel) pair the customer has already funded.

Funding a pair states a ceiling and creates no campaign — money must not start anything on its own. This is the half a PERSON performs: the caller states only what its own screen knows (which brand, which offer, which sales funnel, which acquisition channel), plus an optional `legKey` when the customer funded two legs of the same pair and there are two campaigns to start.

It CANNOT state a workflow, a campaign name or a per-campaign budget: the workflow is campaign-service's choice and is re-picked every run, the name is derived from the identity, and the money is billing's and is already set. campaign-service's body is strict, so a request carrying one of those is refused rather than having it stripped — this gateway forwards the body byte-identical and adds nothing.

A pair that cannot be started is REFUSED with a sentence written for a person, in `error`, alongside a machine-readable `reason` code, under campaign-service's own status (400, 409 or 502). All three reach the caller unchanged: "nothing can run that channel yet", "you haven't funded it" and "this channel doesn't sell that funnel" are three different answers and the customer is owed the right one.

200.description: The pair's campaign. `started: false, alreadyRunning: true` when it was already live; `started: true` when a stopped campaign was started again. Shape owned by campaign-service.

201.description: A campaign was created for the pair and started. Shape owned by campaign-service.

get.summary: Per trigger type, over a window: events fired, ran, skipped (by reason), pending
get.description: Proxy to campaign-service GET /internal/offers/{offerId}/trigger-events/summary. Trigger events (owner 2026-10-09): a REACTIVE leg runs when a trigger fires (a positive reply received, a lead requested, a meeting booked...). Each occurrence is recorded with what it did: `ran` (campaigns run) or `skipped` with one named reason (e.g. `campaign_off`, `no_campaign`, `unfunded`, `run_in_flight`). The org is the authenticated one (never a header/query the caller names). Query forwarded verbatim; campaign-service owns its validation (400) and the body. Status and body relayed verbatim. Groups the offer's events with `occurredAt` in [from, to] (to absent = now) by trigger type; a type with no event in the window is absent. `recordedSince` = when recording started: before it, absence means not recorded.

post.summary: Push an email to send, or fire any trigger: report one occurrence for a person
post.description: Report ONE occurrence of a trigger on your brand and offer, with your own API key. Every live campaign of yours whose reactive step answers that trigger runs for the person named (same funding and rules as any campaign run). Example: push an email you wrote (`triggerId: email_pushed_via_api`, `person.email`, `item: {subject, bodyText}`) and your Email Sending campaign sends it as written from our inboxes. Proxy to campaign-service POST /internal/trigger-events/public: body forwarded as is, status and refusals relayed verbatim. The answer's `event.outcome` says what ran (`ran`) or why not (`skipped` + reason, e.g. `no_campaign`, `unfunded`); a person still being filed leaves the event `pending` a few minutes. Read events back with GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/trigger-events. `performed` is not accepted here (400 `performed_not_reportable`). A trigger the platform computes itself (served `callable: false` by GET /v1/public/channels, e.g. a delay or a poll) cannot be reported: 400 `trigger_not_callable`, nothing recorded.

post.description:

The statement outranks both the matcher's signal and its judgment, survives a re-run of the matcher (it is keyed on the pair, not on a matcher run), and is correctable by restating it or by taking it back with the DELETE on the same path. The pairings themselves and their summary counts are read at GET /v1/leads/crm-pairings?brandId=… and GET /v1/leads/crm-pairing-counts?brandId=…, which this gateway forwards through its single-lead read — the segment is not validated here and the query string travels verbatim, and lead-service registers both literal paths ahead of its own lead-id parameter. The body is forwarded VERBATIM: this gateway does not re-declare, narrow or enumerate lead-service's request shape, so the `ruling` vocabulary stays authoritative in one place and a verdict it adds needs no release here. Its refusals (a missing or non-uuid `brandId`, a missing `crmContactId`, a `leadId` that is not a uuid, a `ruling` outside the vocabulary, a non-string `note`) reach the caller with their own status and body. The caller's org AND user identity are forwarded, because lead-service records WHO ruled. Refer to lead-service openapi.json for the exact request and response shapes.

post.summary: State by hand what happened to one lead at one funnel step (or that it never will)
post.description:
Pass-through to lead-service POST /orgs/leads/{id}/step-statements. Records, by hand, what happened to this lead at one step of its campaign's sales funnel. An `outcome` is written to the same conversion ledger every consumer already counts, so the brand's outcome counts move on the next read with nothing to change downstream; a `never` goes to a store no count reads, so it can never move a number — it exists so a reader can tell a lead that is DEAD at a step from one still PENDING. The body is forwarded VERBATIM: this gateway does not re-declare or narrow lead-service's request shape, and lead-service owns which statements are legal, including its refusals (a `never` on a step that already happened, a value attached to a `never`, an unparseable timestamp). Those refusals reach the caller with their own status and body so a surface can say WHY a statement was refused. The caller's org AND user identity are forwarded, because lead-service records who stated the fact and attributes the statement to the caller's own campaign row. Refer to lead-service openapi.json for the exact request and response shapes.

Request body: documented from lead-service POST /orgs/leads/{id}/step-statements, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

schema.description: The `id` of a lead as returned by GET /v1/leads.

step.description: The step being stated. "meeting_attended" and "website_visit" exist here and nowhere in the tracker: attendance happens off the client's website, and a visit is measured by the delivery layer as a click, so for both only a human can state what those signals missed. A hand-stated visit ADDS to the measured one and never suppresses it: a lead carrying both is counted once, because the hand-stated row is left out of the counts. The legacy spelling "purchase" is accepted and normalized to "sale".

kind.description: outcome — this happened; it is written to the conversion ledger every consumer already counts, so the brand's counts move on the next read. never — this will NOT happen; it is NOT an outcome, nothing counts it anywhere, and it exists so a consumer can tell a lead that is DEAD at a step from one still PENDING.

valueCents.description: What the outcome was worth, in cents. REQUIRED on a "sale" outcome and optional on every other step: a won deal is the one place estimating has no excuse, because with no value every downstream money figure prices it at the brand's average lifetime revenue, which describes no real customer. Stating it early on an unusually large lead, long before it closes, is exactly why the other steps keep it optional. Rejected with 400 on a "never" statement rather than silently dropped.

costCents.description: What this step cost YOU, in cents — MANDATORY on every statement, outcome and "never" alike. The platform automates the first leg and you perform the rest (you run the meeting, you close the deal), so you are the only one who can say what that leg cost; without it a cost of acquisition counts only the leg we billed for and every return shown for it is too good. You choose what goes in: zero, your time valued however you like, real expenses. ZERO IS A LEGITIMATE ANSWER and reads back as a stated zero — leaving the field out is a 400 (code cost_required), never a zero, because an absent cost and a stated zero must stay distinguishable. Negative is a 400. THIS MONEY IS YOURS: it is recorded because you told us, it is never charged to you, and it never enters the platform's own spend ledger or your billing. A "never" carries one too — a meeting that was run and went nowhere still cost what it cost.

causedByOutreach.description: WHOSE win it was — did OUR outreach cause this, or something else you already do? true — ours. false — yours (a referral, a conference, your existing pipeline, another agency): the outcome is REAL, it is recorded and counted among your own exactly like any other, and stating it honestly costs you nothing; it simply stops it inflating the return we report on our own outreach. LEAVING IT OUT IS NOT "NOT US": an absent answer is recorded as "nobody was asked" and stays distinguishable from both answers forever, which is why every statement made before this existed reads as unstated rather than silently acquiring an answer nobody gave. Optional on every step; rejected with 400 on a "never" statement (nothing happened, so nothing caused it). A restatement REPLACES the statement, so restating without naming a cause returns it to unstated.

note.description: Free text the person stating the fact wrote, stored verbatim.
note.example: Closed on the call, contract signed 2026-08-19.

occurredAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of WHEN the outcome happened, for a fact stated after the fact — it is what the by-day series buckets on. Unparseable values are a 400, never silently replaced by now().

Withdrawing what is already withdrawn is a success, not an error. `id` and `step` are the ones the caller already holds, and neither is validated here: lead-service owns the step vocabulary and this gateway does not enumerate it, so a step it ships later needs no release here. Its refusals reach the caller with their own status and body, `code` included — a step nobody stated and only READS as reached because the funnel implies it, an outcome the tracker reported rather than a person, a pair outside this org — so a surface can tell each apart from a server failure. post.summary: State when the next follow-up to one lead is owed
post.description:
Pass-through to lead-service POST /orgs/leads/{id}/followups. States what was done for this person and when the next action is due — which is how a customer looking at a lead whose next answer is days away can say it is owed NOW: the write sets the due date and releases any claim, so the campaign picks that person up on its next turn instead of waiting the schedule out. The response IS the resulting state, so a caller never has to ask what its write did. `id` is the `id` a row of GET /v1/leads already carries — the same one the detail panel used to read the lead — so no identity field about the person is re-supplied. The body is forwarded VERBATIM: this gateway does not re-declare, narrow or enumerate lead-service's request shape, and lead-service owns which statements are legal, including its refusals (a date outside the accepted range, an unparseable one, a missing reason on a stop, a lead outside this org). Those refusals reach the caller with their own status and body, `code` included, so a surface can say WHY the request was refused rather than showing a generic failure. The caller's org AND user identity are forwarded; the org boundary is the authenticated one and is never read from the body or query. Refer to lead-service openapi.json for the exact request and response shapes.

Request body: documented from lead-service POST /orgs/leads/{id}/followups, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

kind.description: handed — the thread is a PERSON's now (the client was asked to answer, the reply was escalated, a human answered); reason (required) says to whom / why; PERMANENT: no automated responder claims the row again and a later scheduled leaves the due date NULL. scheduled — we owe this person an action at dueAt (the first enqueue after qualification, and the re-enqueue after a fresh reply has been re-qualified); it is not an action, so the count does not move. acted — a worker answered them, and nextDueAt says when the next answer is owed; this is the only kind that increments the count. stopped — nothing is owed right now, and reason says why; NOT a tombstone, a later scheduled re-enters the person, which is exactly how "they answered again" is expressed.

dueAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp, REQUIRED on kind=scheduled. Bounded, never clamped: a date in the past or further out than a year is a 400 carrying the accepted range, because silently answering a request nobody made would leave the caller believing its date was honoured.

nextDueAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp, REQUIRED on kind=acted: when the NEXT action is owed. This service does not compute it. The interval is chosen per lead by the worker — a prospect who writes "recontact me in January" must be honoured — so it is stored data, not a ladder, and the growing intervals are what limit the sequence rather than a cap on the number of follow-ups (there is none).

reason.description: REQUIRED on kind=stopped and kind=handed: why nothing is owed right now, stated by the caller and stored verbatim ("answered_again", "meeting_booked", "not_interested"). Absent is a 400, never an empty string.

llmAlias.description: kind=acted ONLY (any other kind with it = 400 llm_alias_only_on_acted). BEST-TPL-LLM-1022-LS: the LLM alias the acting run wrote this message with, as resolved for the run (e.g. features-service writer-pick). Stored on the act and served on GET /internal/leads/{leadId}/sent-messages as writtenBy.llmAlias. Optional: absent = the run states none (served as unknown with a reason, never guessed). Trimmed, 1..200 chars.

get.description:
Proxy to brand-service GET /orgs/brands/{brandId}/offers. An OFFER is one thing the brand sells; its id is what offer-scoped routes take (economics, steps, documents, sales funnels, campaigns). Archived offers are hidden unless `includeArchived=true`. Query string forwarded verbatim; status and body owned by brand-service.

Response: documented from brand-service GET /orgs/brands/{brandId}/offers, which owns it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

Proxy to brand-service GET /orgs/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}. Query string forwarded verbatim; status and body owned by brand-service.

Response: documented from brand-service GET /orgs/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}, which owns it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

Proxy to brand-service GET /orgs/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/documents. Documents are files the client owns about ONE offer (a one-pager, a case study, a spec sheet, an FAQ), sent as an email attachment on a reply to a prospect. Uploading one changes no campaign by itself: a document is attached only (a) when you reply yourself with `POST /v1/replies` and list it in `attachments` [{ document_id }], or (b) by a WORKFLOW that attaches offer documents, reading this list (fileName + description) to pick the file that helps. Which workflow a campaign's pipe runs is chosen by its PLAY, not by you directly: to make a campaign's AI meeting booking replies carry an attachment, find (`GET /v1/tactics?q=attach`) or create (`POST /v1/tactics`) a tactic describing that attachment behaviour, a strategy requiring it (`POST /v1/strategies`), add it as a play on the pipe `ai-meeting-booking|conversation_to_meeting_booked` (`POST /v1/plays`), then pick a sales funnel running that play (`GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels`, its id carries `@ai-meeting-booking~<strategy id>`) and launch it with `POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns`. Write each description as when the file helps a prospect. Accepted: pdf, docx, pptx, xlsx, doc, ppt, xls, csv, txt, md, png, jpg/jpeg, gif, webp; at most 5 MB per file and 25 files per offer. The file extension decides the type and must match the content. Answers { documents }, oldest first, metadata only (no file bytes).

put.summary: Set a brand's sales rep phone

Proxy to brand-service PUT /orgs/brands/{brandId}/sales-rep-phone. States (or changes) the one number to ring when a sales interest lands on this brand. salesRepPhone.description: The number to ring when a sales interest lands on this brand. Accepts any typed format (spaces, dashes, parentheses, dots) as long as it carries a country code — either a leading `+` or the international `00` prefix — and is 8-15 digits. Stored in strict E.164 (`+33770657585`). A national number with no country code is rejected 400: no country is inferred, because a guess dials a different person.

put.description:
The single endpoint for modifying a workflow. Behavior depends on what you send:

**Metadata only** (no `dag` in body): updates description/tags in-place. Returns 200 with `_action: 'updated'`.

**DAG with same signature**: the DAG structure hasn't changed (e.g. only config tweaks that don't affect the hash). Updates in-place. Returns 200 with `_action: 'updated'`.

**DAG with new signature**: creates a new workflow in a new dynasty (fork). The original workflow is kept active unless its entire dynasty has zero campaign runs, in which case it is deprecated. Returns 201 with `_action: 'forked'`, plus `_forkedFromName`, `_forkedFromId`, and `_sourceDynastyDeprecated`.

Returns 409 if an active workflow with the same DAG signature already exists, with `existingWorkflowId` and `existingWorkflowSlug` in the response body.

post.summary: Fork a workflow version with a stated change
post.description: Transparent proxy to workflow-service POST /workflows/{id}/fork. The copy branches from exactly this version. Copies a workflow with a stated change into a NEW dynasty. `changes` is a JSON Patch (RFC 6902: `add`, `replace`, `remove`, `test`) applied in order to a copy of the source DAG (`{nodes, edges}`, read it with GET /v1/workflows/{id}); everything it does not name stays byte-identical. Under `/nodes` a non-numeric path segment names a node by its `id`, e.g. `{ op: "add", path: "/nodes/fetch-lead/config/body", value: {...} }`. The copy is validated like any stored workflow, deployed, and serves every pipe its source serves (active at once); the source is never modified. Optional `description` (defaults to the source's: say what the copy does differently, workflows are judged on their DAG and description) and `tags`. Responses come back from workflow-service verbatim: 201 `{ workflow, sourceWorkflow, changesApplied }`; 400 change leaves the DAG identical or the result is invalid; 404; 409 the same copy already exists (`existingWorkflowId`, so a re-run is idempotent); 422 a change cannot apply (`changeIndex`).

post.summary: Stream chat response (SSE)
post.description:
Send a message and receive a streamed AI response via Server-Sent Events (SSE).

**Session lifecycle:**
- To start a new conversation, **omit `sessionId`**. The first SSE event will be `data: {"sessionId":"<uuid>"}` — store this ID.
- To continue a conversation, pass that `sessionId` in subsequent requests.
- If a provided `sessionId` does not exist or belongs to a different org, the stream returns an error and closes.

**SSE event order:**
Each `data:` line contains a JSON object. Events arrive in this order:

1. **Session** — `{"sessionId":"<uuid>"}` (always first)
2. **Thinking** *(optional)* — `thinking_start` → one or more `thinking_delta` → `thinking_stop`
3. **Tokens** — `{"type":"token","content":"..."}` streamed incrementally
4. **Tool calls** *(optional, repeatable)* — `tool_call` followed by `tool_result`, then more thinking/tokens as the AI continues
5. **Input request** *(optional)* — `input_request` when the AI needs structured user input
6. **Buttons** *(optional)* — `{"type":"buttons","buttons":[...]}` with quick-reply options
7. **Error** *(optional)* — `{"type":"error","message":"..."}` when the model returns an empty response (e.g. context overflow, safety filter). Always followed by `[DONE]`.
8. **Done** — `"[DONE]"` (always last)

See the SSE event schemas (SSESessionEvent, SSETokenEvent, SSEToolCallEvent, etc.) for exact payload shapes.

200.description: SSE stream of chat events. Each `data:` line is a JSON object matching one of the SSE event schemas (SSESessionEvent, SSETokenEvent, SSEThinkingStartEvent, SSEThinkingDeltaEvent, SSEThinkingStopEvent, SSEToolCallEvent, SSEToolResultEvent, SSEInputRequestEvent, SSEButtonsEvent, SSEErrorEvent), except the final `data: "[DONE]"` which is a plain string.

post.summary: Pay what a postpaid account owes now
post.description: Charges the org's saved card, off-session, for exactly the amount the postpaid account owes (billing-service computes it; no body). Transparent proxy to billing-service POST /v1/accounts/pay_balance: status and body forwarded verbatim. Refusals carry a stable `code` and, where relevant, `owed_cents`: 402 `charge_declined`; 409 `not_postpaid`, `balance_below_minimum_charge`, `no_chargeable_payment_method`, `card_not_chargeable_off_session`; 429 `charge_backoff`; 502 `upstream_error`; 404 no billing account. Body and status forwarded verbatim.

200.description: Minimums in force — pass-through from billing-service

post.summary: What the browser needs to render this org's card form
post.description: Asks billing-service how THIS org's acquirer saves a card and passes the descriptor through untouched: `hosted_redirect` (send the customer to `url`) or `embedded_widget` (load `script_url`, initialise with the per-order PUBLIC `token`, mount the card field). No merchant credential is included — the card is typed in an iframe the acquirer hosts and never touches the page or this gateway. Nobody is charged for adding a card. Request body is forwarded verbatim; the fields documented here are the ones billing accepts today, not a whitelist.

get.summary: Does this org have a saved, chargeable card?
get.description: Read live from whichever acquirer holds the org's cards. THREE answers, kept apart on purpose: 200 `{saved:true, method}` there is one; 200 `{saved:false, reason}` the acquirer answered and there is none; 502 we could not ask at all. A caller that collapses the last two would either tell a customer to re-enter a card we already hold, or arm a recurring charge off a timeout — so the gateway forwards the downstream status and body as they are.

200.description: The acquirer answered — pass-through from billing-service

delete.description: Removes the calling org's saved card. billing-service collects what is owed FIRST, on the card that is about to go, then removes it whatever that collection did — the gateway adds no ordering, no pre-check and no retry. Refused for nobody: no balance, no debt state and no failed charge blocks it, and an org with no card is not an error. Nothing is forgiven — a debt that could not be collected stays owed. The org is the authenticated one; a caller cannot name someone else's. Response is billing-service's, forwarded field-for-field.

get.summary: Free credits this org is still waiting on

Normal org auth (same tier as GET /v1/billing/credits/grants); billing-service scopes the response to the caller's x-org-id, so an org reads only its own promises and the client never names an org. One page of tactics (id, name, description, how many workflows were judged on it and how many follow it). Query string forwarded verbatim (documented today: q, limit; not a whitelist). A TACTIC is a yes/no tag our judge puts on every workflow version, judged on the tactic's description (for example "Catch-all": sends to addresses whose mail server accepts every address). A STRATEGY is a rule over tactics: the tactics a workflow must follow (`requires`) and must not follow (`excludes`), for example "Valid + Catch-all". A PLAY is a pipe x a strategy (a pipe is one channel x one leg, id `<channel slug>|<leg key>`, e.g. `sales-cold-email-outreach|lead_found_to_website_visit`): the pipe runs only the workflows its strategy allows, picked by ROI. Every pipe has a default play (id = the bare pipe id); another play's id is `<pipe id>~<strategy id>`. This catalogue is shared by every client: read it before creating, names and descriptions are unique fleet-wide. It is HOW you change what a campaign does (for example "its AI meeting booking replies carry an offer document as an attachment"): (1) a tactic naming the behaviour (`GET /v1/tactics?q=...` first, else `POST /v1/tactics`); (2) a strategy requiring it (`POST /v1/strategies`); (3) a play = that strategy on the pipe that should behave so (`POST /v1/plays`, e.g. pipe `ai-meeting-booking|conversation_to_meeting_booked`); (4) a sales funnel running that play: in `GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels` each pipe of a funnel id reads `<leg>@<channel>` for its default play and `<leg>@<channel>~<strategy id>` for another play; (5) a sales funnel campaign on that funnel (`POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns`, create it with `status: stopped`, then run it when the client agrees). An existing campaign keeps its own funnel and plays: a new behaviour is a new campaign. A new tactic is judged on every workflow within minutes; a strategy no workflow follows yet runs nothing (its play shows `runnable: false`). A new tactic reaches no older strategy by itself: a strategy that names nothing about it lets its workflows through either way, so exclude it (or require it) there. Editing a strategy's tactics or description is staff only (`PATCH /v1/strategies/{id}`), because it changes what every client's campaigns on its plays run. Byte passthrough to features-service; status and body (including 400/404/409 with a named `reason`) owned by it.

Forward it verbatim. Rendered to the model in the same "Checks we ran on their company" block as a campaign email (context only). companyDomain.description: The recipient's company website or domain.

headline.description: The recipient's own one-line professional headline.

bodyText.description: The first email of the sequence the product would send, as plain text.

model.description: Resolved model id that wrote the email.

promptType.description: The prompt template that wrote the email: the best mature cold-email workflow's, when it was written.

modelAlias.description: The model alias the workflow states (e.g. glm-pro). null on a preview stored before the preview followed the best mature workflow.

workflowSlug.description: The workflow whose template + model wrote the email (the best mature cold-email workflow at the time). null on a preview stored before the preview followed it.

text.description: A sentence or clause of bodyText, verbatim.

start.description: Offset of text in bodyText (JS string index): bodyText.slice(start, end) === text.

kind.description: Where the reason comes from. prospect: a fact about the recipient or their company (the data sent in `recipient`). brand: a fact about the sender's company, read from its website by brand-service. audience: the segment sent in `audience`. instruction: a writing rule of the email template (greeting, diagnostic question, call to action), not a fact.

source.description: The exact input: `recipient.<field>`, `check.<n>` (the n-th check of `qualification`), `audience`, `brand.name`, `brand.<extracted field key>` (e.g. brand.customerPainPoints), or `instruction`.

sourceValue.description: The input's actual value as the model received it. null for instruction.

reason.description: Why this text is there, in one sentence, as reported by the model that wrote the email.

highlights.description: Why each sentence of bodyText exists and which input it rests on, in body order, non-overlapping. Reported by a SECOND completion that reads the finished email (the writing call is the plain /generate call), then checked here: every text is verbatim in bodyText and every source is an input actually sent; anything failing a check is dropped, so a sentence may carry no highlight. null when that second call failed (the email is served anyway) or for a preview stored before highlights existed.

trigger.description: A REACTIVE path/funnel starts with this trigger (unique slug, unique name; owner 2026-10-11): `line` reads it in place of the trigger step. Null on a proactive one (it starts at Start).

triggerLabel.description: A REACTIVE funnel: the customer label of what starts it (e.g. `Positive replies`), shown as a tag. Null on a proactive funnel.

type.description: `proactive` when at least one pipe is proactive (own budget, worked every tick), else `reactive`. A funnel HEADED by a trigger (id `trigger:<id>+...`, owner 2026-10-15) is always `reactive`: every pipe answers its trigger, proactive pipes included. Campaign-service and billing relay it; nobody re-grades pipe modes.

face.description: Path of the name's face SVG on this service (`GET /public/catalogue/faces/{name}.svg`).

line.description: Who works each leg, in order.

costUsd.description: Average fleet cost, in the unit `costPer` names. Null unless `status` is measured or estimated.

costPer.description: The unit of `costUsd` in words, on every row: `per <outcome step>` for a step, pipe, channel (its best pipe's step) or workflow (its pipe's step), e.g. `per positive reply`; `per paying client` for a sales path or funnel. Quote it with the figure. Null when `costUsd` is null.

roi.description: Average fleet return multiple. Null unless measured or estimated.

roiBasis.description: `estimated` when anything the ROI rests on is not a measured fleet outcome: every ROI today, since it divides a step value or a lifetime revenue that ends on the fleet median of STATED lifetime revenues. Null with no roi.

status.description: About the COST. `measured`: every input is a measured fleet outcome (a pipe's, step's, channel's or workflow's cost per outcome is the mature fleet figure). `estimated` (sales funnels and paths): the pipes' costs are measured but a leg RATE the cost per paying client uses is not (an industry default or a declared rate): never present it as measured. `learning`: no mature history, cost and roi null. `customer_time`: the customer's own team, no cost to us. Rows rank by this tier first (measured > estimated > customer_time > learning), then roi desc: a measured figure is never out-ranked by an estimate.
Always `expected`: an assumption-backed figure, never measured. Show it with an `expected` mark.

costUsd.description: Expected cost per paying client, USD.

costPer.description: `per paying client`; null when `costUsd` is null.

roi.description: Expected return multiple: (lifetime revenue - what the people it takes over were already worth) / expected cost per paying client.

basis.description: The WEAKEST input it rests on (measured < stated < fleet < default). Null with no figure.

unavailableReason.description: Why there is no figure: `no_lifetime_revenue`, `leg_unrated:<leg>`, `pipe_unpriced:<pipe id>`, `leg_without_pipe:<leg>`, `customer_time_only` (nothing of ours costs anything), `takeover_step_unvalued` (cost served, roi null). Null with a figure.

expected.description: EXPECTED economics (owner 2026-10-11: a ROI is never blank, an assumption if need be): the funnel formula where every missing input takes an assumption. Pipe cost: mature workflow > seeded default > market benchmark > its early flash figure > another channel's mature price on the same leg (the highest); the customer's team costs 0. Leg rate: the path's (brand measured / stated > default) > entry default. On a measured/estimated funnel it equals `costUsd`/`roi`.

runnable.description: We run it today: published, and worked by the customer's own team or on a MANAGED channel (a workflow exists). An unmanaged channel is listed but campaign-service refuses its launch (409 `no_workflow`). A customer surface shows only `runnable` objects.

mixed.description: A proactive pipe AND a reactive pipe we run (platform-operated) in one funnel: its budget caps both, so the reactive part can starve the proactive one (owner 2026-10-10). A mixed funnel is never `runnable`; propose a proactive funnel and a separate reactive one.

ownRateLegs.description: Legs priced on the brand's own rate.

offer.description: Present on a per-offer read only.

stated.description: false = the offer never stated its steps: nothing is set aside.

steps.description: The steps the offer's business has (null when never stated).

alwaysPresent.description: Steps every business has by definition (Lead found, Paid client), counted present.

offerSteps.description: Per-offer read only (owner 2026-10-12): what the offer stated about the steps its business has.

missingSteps.description: The steps of this row the offer's business does not have: ask the client about them before proposing it.

setAside.description: Per-offer read only: the rows matching every other filter but walking a step the offer lacks (same order and limit as `rows`). Never proposable as is.

setAsideByStep.description: Per-offer read only: each missing step and how many set-aside rows it accounts for, most first.

event.description: The conversion that happened on the client's website. "sale" is the terminal "a customer paid" signal (carries a revenue value in valueCents). Idempotency: exact-match on (quote_opportunity_id, sorted brand_ids[]) — co-branded [A,B] is distinct from solo [A]. Body + response shapes are owned by the downstream service.

Request body: documented from journalists-quotes-service POST /orgs/opportunities/{id}/reply, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

audienceId.description: The id of the PERSISTED audience row (status 'suggested', inactive). The caller activates a chosen candidate via PATCH /orgs/audiences/{id}/status {status:'active'}.

name.description: Short human label for this audience (<=4 words), shared across providers — the layer-1 name.

rationale.description: One-sentence description of who this audience targets.

provider.description: Always 'apollo' — apollo-service owns the faithful filters; the candidate commits to apollo.

apolloAudienceId.description: Pointer to the faithful Apollo audience apollo-service built + persisted for this audience.

filters.description: The faithful Apollo filter object (opaque — apollo-service owns its shape), cached on the persisted audience row.

count.description: The audience's live match count (free apollo dry-run snapshot from apollo-service).

status.description: Always 'suggested' (inactive) for a freshly-suggested audience.

validationError.description: Retained for response-shape stability. apollo-service confirms a real audience (or fails loud), so always null.

truncated.description: Reserved for response compatibility. Layer 1 has no hard cap, so freshly suggested candidates return false.

degraded.description: The chooser's verdict: true when NO attempt apollo-service explored really answered the request and it picked the least-bad one anyway. INFORMATION only — a degraded audience is served, persisted and activatable exactly like any other; the customer decides whether to keep it. A candidate is always returned; this never withholds one.

name.description: The layer-1 audience name that failed to build.

reason.description: The underlying error message (apollo-service build or chooser failure).

failedSegments.description: Retained for response-shape stability (the split returns later). Layer 1 emits ONE audience today, so a failed build FAILS the request LOUD (502 carrying the underlying reason) rather than returning an empty list — this array is therefore always empty on a 200.

post.summary: Propose a split of a target audience into segments
post.description:
Proxy to human-service POST /orgs/audiences/split. Turns a target sentence into up to a few non-overlapping segments; persists nothing. One LLM call plus a typed judgment, so it can take up to a minute. Request + response shapes are owned by human-service. Downstream status and body (400 validation, 502 on an LLM error) are forwarded verbatim.

Request body: documented from human-service POST /orgs/audiences/split, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

Response: documented from human-service POST /orgs/audiences/split, which owns it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

targetAudience.description: The confirmed free-text answer to 'who do you sell to?' (e.g. 'B2B SaaS founders in the US and Europe').

axes.description: The axes the segments partition the target along: empty when a single segment is returned, one axis, or two axes crossed. Only axes a people search can filter on.

name.description: Short label, max 4 words, unique within the proposal.

description.description: One plain-language sentence that fully specifies the segment on its own (who, where, what kind of company, plus this segment's partition value). Becomes the audience's description on confirm.

icon.description: Phosphor icon name (kebab-case) from a closed vocabulary; `globe-hemisphere-west` renders as <GlobeHemisphereWest /> in @phosphor-icons/react.

iconConfidence.description: The judge's own certainty about the icon (decorative: the icon is always set).

estimatedLeadCount.description: Approximate number of people (decision-makers matching the segment) it would reach in a large B2B contact database, estimated by the same generation that writes the segments: no search runs, so it is available instantly with the cards. Right order of magnitude only; the real people-search count is measured after confirm. null when no estimate could be made, never 0.

segments.description: 1 to 6 mutually exclusive segments that together cover the target. Nothing is persisted.

post.summary: Create the kept segments of a split as audiences
post.description:
Proxy to human-service POST /orgs/audiences/split/confirm. Creates the segments the customer kept as audiences under (brand, offer), all or nothing. Request + response shapes are owned by human-service. Downstream status and body (400, 409 name conflict) are forwarded verbatim.

Request body: documented from human-service POST /orgs/audiences/split/confirm, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

Response: documented from human-service POST /orgs/audiences/split/confirm, which owns it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

offerId.description: The brand-service offer the new audiences belong to. Stored verbatim, like brandId.

targetAudience.description: The confirmed target the segments were split from, in the customer's words. Restated as a person-level target (who to write to given what this offer sells, the people around them, and the functions that are out) and stored as each audience's nlPrompt.

segments.description: The segments the customer kept (at least one). Pass them back as returned by /orgs/audiences/split; icon fields are accepted and ignored.

description.description: One-sentence summary of who THIS audience targets, distinct from the shared batch nlPrompt. LLM-generated at /suggest time. null for rows predating this field.

apolloAudienceId.description: Pointer to the faithful Apollo audience owned by apollo-service ('one filter vocabulary' Wave 2). Set for apollo audiences; null for apify (legacy) rows and pre-Wave-2 rows not yet backfilled. The faithful filters live in apollo-service; the `filters` field below is human-service's opaque cache of them.

crmUploadId.description: The ONE imported CRM source (crm-service upload id) this audience is bound to. When set, every CRM serve made under this audience is restricted to the people that came from that file, so several CRM audiences can coexist for one brand and each behaves as its own audience. null = unbound ⟹ the serve covers the brand's whole imported list (the pre-existing behaviour).

segment.description: A part of the brand's own CRM, as crm-service's PeopleSegment states it (passed through verbatim, validated by crm-service): dealStages [{stage, pipeline?}], dealStatuses, tags, reached / notReached (funnel steps), includeClients, includeOptedOut. Lists OR, keys AND; clients and opted-out people are out unless stated. Names come from crm-service GET /orgs/contacts/segments.

crmPeople.description: The PEOPLE-pool filter this CRM audience is bound to: every serve draws from the brand's merged people (everyone its connected tools know, one row per human) who match it, instead of from imported files. null = not people-bound (file-bound via crmUploadId, or the whole imported list).

crmPeopleByStage.description: A people-bound CRM audience whose segment names dealStages: crm-service's counts per stated stage (same snapshot as Size / Remaining). Entries overlap when a person holds deals at two of them. null otherwise.

offerId.description: The offer (Org > Brand > Offer > Campaign) this audience belongs to — an id owned by brand-service. An audience is assembled for one distinct thing the brand sells, so it is scoped to that offer rather than to every offer of the brand. null = no offer stated ⟹ the audience is brand-wide, the pre-existing behaviour.

status.description: Always 'suggested' (inactive) for a freshly-suggested audience.

profileAudienceId.description: The client PROFILE (WHO, a cold audience the client keeps or pauses on the Targeting page) this source list was built for: a buying-signal list (hiring now, new in role, recently funded) or a competitor-post engagement list finds THAT profile's people, screened against the profile's text. Pausing or archiving the profile pauses its lists; resuming it resumes them (unless the source itself is off). null on a profile itself, on a whole-ICP list built before profiles had their own (retired once they do), and on every other audience. Show profiles = rows with null here and channels[0].list = apollo_search; sources = channels[0].list.

canonicalAudienceId.description: When this audience is a deprecated provider-variant (e.g. retired '<base> [Apify]' from the apify->apollo migration), the id of its active canonical replacement. Membership/stats reads resolve a deprecated match to this audience. null for non-deprecated / unlinked rows.

avatarUrl.description: Audience avatar as a hosted HTTP(S) URL. null until generated.

degraded.description: The chooser's verdict on the audience it picked for this row: true when no attempt apollo-service explored really answered the request and the least-bad one was chosen anyway. INFORMATION for the customer and the dashboard — nothing here blocks, filters or warns on it, and an audience is always chosen. false for rows created before the flag existed and whenever the chooser judged the pick a genuine answer.

targetText.description: THE text of this audience: who the customer wants for THIS audience, in plain language. It is the text to show as the audience AND the text the pre-pay screen (Jev) judges every lead of every list below against, before any paid reveal. Distinct from nlPrompt, which a split shares across all its sibling audiences. null ⟹ see targetTextMissingReason.

targetTextOrigin.description: How targetText was written. segment_target: this audience is one of several split from one shared target, and the text was drafted for this audience alone from that target + its own segment. audience_target: the audience is not one of several, so its nlPrompt IS its text. null when targetText is null.

targetTextMissingReason.description: Why targetText is null. no_customer_text: the audience holds no customer text at all (no nlPrompt), so there is nothing to judge leads against. not_written_yet: the text is being drafted (it is written before the audience's first serve; until then the screen judges against nlPrompt and records that it did). null when targetText is set.

channel.description: The outreach channel that uses this list. cold_email is the only channel today.

list.description: What the list is. apollo_search: an Apollo people search. apollo_buying_signal: the same search narrowed to people showing a buying signal (see signal). linkedin_engagement: people who engaged with competitor LinkedIn posts (see signal). crm_contacts: the client's own uploaded contacts. apify_search: legacy search provider.

post.summary: Estimate how many people each proposed segment holds
post.description:
Proxy to human-service POST /orgs/audiences/split/estimate. Body { brandId, offerId?, segments: [{ name, description }] } (1 to 8 segments); returns { estimates: [{ name, estimatedPeople, unavailableReason }] }. Persists nothing. Request + response shapes are owned by human-service. Downstream status and body (400 validation, 502 on an outage) are forwarded verbatim.

Request body: documented from human-service POST /orgs/audiences/split/estimate, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

Response: documented from human-service POST /orgs/audiences/split/estimate, which owns it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

offerId.description: The offer the segments were proposed for. Accepted for attribution in logs; it does not change the estimate.

segments.description: The proposed segments as returned by /orgs/audiences/split (or /orgs/audiences/suggest): name + description each, 1 to 8. Extra fields (icon, estimatedLeadCount) are accepted and ignored.

estimatedPeople.description: Approximate number of people with a verified email in Apollo who match a quick draft of Apollo People Search filters written from the segment sentence (one cheap LLM call for the whole list, then one free count per segment). Similar-title matching is switched off, so title-based segments are not inflated (~10x) by Apollo's similar titles. Rounded to 2 significant figures. An order of magnitude to show on a card, NOT the audience's final count: the confirmed audience runs its own full build, whose count can differ. null only when unavailableReason is set.

unavailableReason.description: Why no number could be measured for this segment (null when estimatedPeople is set): no_filters_drafted = the model wrote no filters for it, twice; filters_rejected = the search refused its filters, twice.

estimates.description: One entry per requested segment, in request order. Nothing is persisted, no audience is created.

post.summary: Create a buying-signal audience
post.description:
Proxy to human-service POST /orgs/audiences/signal. Creates an audience of people showing a buying signal (first type: linkedin_engagement, people who engaged with competitor LinkedIn posts). Body { brandId, offerId?, name?, nlPrompt, status?, signal: { type, windowDays, competitorPages? } }; the body's brandId is also forwarded as the x-brand-id identity header. Request + response shapes are owned by human-service. Downstream status and body (400, 409 name conflict, the signal provider's named 4xx such as a malformed competitor page) are forwarded verbatim.

Request body: documented from human-service POST /orgs/audiences/signal, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

offerId.description: The brand-service offer this audience belongs to. Stored verbatim, like brandId. Omitted = brand-wide.

name.description: Audience name (English), unique per (brand, offer). Omitted = apollo-service's label (competitor slugs + window).

nlPrompt.description: Who among the engagers is worth writing to, in plain English (people, not only companies). Stored as the audience target: the pre-pay screen judges every engager teaser (name, title, headline, employer) against it before any email is paid for.

status.description: Initial status. Omitted = active.

windowDays.description: Age of the competitor posts whose engagers are served, in days, counted back from each serve (rolling).

competitorPages.description: 1-3 competitor LinkedIn company page URLs (https://www.linkedin.com/company/<slug>/). Validated by apollo-service, whose named 400 is relayed.

filters.description: Apollo base filters. Must be empty: apollo-service refuses Apollo filters beside this signal with a named 400 (relayed), since its people are LinkedIn engagers, not an Apollo search. Omitted = {}.

201.description: Created audience (human-service { audience })

post.summary: Build the active audience portfolio of a brand + offer from its ICP
post.description:
Proxy to human-service POST /orgs/audiences/portfolio. Derives the active audiences (cold split audiences + buying-signal audiences) for a brand + offer from the ICP text the customer validated. Answers once the cold audiences exist (seconds) with status "building"; the buying-signal audiences finish in the background and flip it to "ready". Poll the same POST until ready: a replay of the same brand + offer returns the current set without re-spending. The gateway waits up to 10 minutes upstream. Request + response shapes are owned by human-service; downstream status and body (400, 409, 502) are forwarded verbatim.

Request body: documented from human-service POST /orgs/audiences/portfolio, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

Response: documented from human-service POST /orgs/audiences/portfolio, which owns it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

offerId.description: The brand-service offer every portfolio audience belongs to. Stored verbatim, like brandId.

targetAudience.description: The ICP text the customer validated (who they sell to), in their words. Every portfolio audience is derived from it, and every one carries the same person-level restatement of it as its nlPrompt (the target the pre-pay screen judges each teaser against).

status.description: building = the cold audiences are live and the buying-signal audiences are still being measured in the background (call again to read them; nothing is re-spent); ready = every signal has its outcome.

replayed.description: true when this (brand, offer) portfolio was already launched (or in flight) and the recorded set is returned; nothing new was created.

target.description: The nlPrompt every portfolio audience carries.

ABSENT (with availableToContactCount / availableToContactPct) for a linkedin_engagement audience whose pool is unknown: no provider count exists for it until serve-next has walked it to exhaustion, after which it is that walked pool.

availableToContactCount.description: Pool members NOT suppressed within the 3-month re-contact window (never-served, or last served >3 months ago). Computed server-side from the same per-brand cross-provider suppression the serve path enforces.

availableToContactPct.description: round(availableToContactCount / sizeCount * 100), integer 0..100. 0 when sizeCount is 0. Denominator is exactly sizeCount so Size and Remaining stay coherent.

post.summary: Add one person to my CRM (one contact, email optional)
post.description:
Add ONE person you know to a brand's CRM contacts, by JSON: the way to put a specific prospect (a name you were given, someone met at an event, a LinkedIn profile) in front of your campaigns without a CSV. Give `brandId` and at least one of: an `email`, a `linkedinUrl` (linkedin.com profile), or a name (`fullName`, or `firstName` + `lastName`) WITH a company (`companyName` or `companyDomain`). Optional: `phone`, `jobTitle`, `note` (what you know about the person, up to 5000 characters). The email is OPTIONAL: a contact with an email can be written to at once; a contact without one is looked up only when a campaign serves it (no lookup, no cost at add time), and its `emailStatus` reads `unknown` until then (`not_found` if the lookup found none). Adding the same person twice (same email or same LinkedIn) returns the SAME contact with the new details merged in (200, `created: false`, `matchedOn`); a new person answers 201. The person joins the brand's list "Contacts added one by one" (GET /v1/orgs/contacts/uploads, `kind: manual`). Proxy to crm-service POST /orgs/contacts; status and body piped byte-identical, refusals forwarded verbatim (400 `type: validation` for a bad field, 400 `type: not_enough_to_find` when the person cannot be identified). Requires a user (x-user-id).

Request body: documented from crm-service POST /orgs/contacts, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

companyDomain.description: A domain or a URL (ntt.com, https://www.ntt.com/...).

note.description: What the client knows about the person ("I met him at X"), stored with the contact for the email writer.

schema.description: Needs an email, a LinkedIn URL, or a name with a company (companyName or companyDomain).

post.summary: Serve the next batch of un-served contacts for a brand
post.description:
Proxy to crm-service POST /orgs/contacts/serve-next. Request body forwarded verbatim — crm-service owns its shape. Response shape owned by crm-service.

Request body: documented from crm-service POST /orgs/contacts/serve-next, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

limit.description: Max contacts to serve this call. Defaults to 100.

uploadIds.description: Restrict the serve to these imported CRM files (ids from GET /orgs/contacts/uploads). Omit for the whole brand. Suppression stays brand-wide: a contact already served through another file is never returned again, whichever file is used.

signedUp.description: true = only people who signed up to the brand's product (its auth provider, e.g. Clerk); false = only people who did not.

replied.description: false = only people who NEVER wrote to the brand on any conversation channel (Gmail / WhatsApp / LinkedIn inbound, any answer to our cold email): never written to, or written to without an answer. true = only people who answered. Copilot / API use is the product being used, not a conversation.

reachableBy.description: Only people holding a phone / an email (a list = all).

dealStages.description: CRM pipeline stage: the person has a deal CURRENTLY at one of these stages (the customer's own stage name, optionally its pipeline name; trimmed, case-insensitive). Names come from GET /orgs/contacts/segments.

dealStatuses.description: The deal's CRM status, verbatim (GoHighLevel: open, won, lost, abandoned). With dealStages, the SAME deal must match both.

tags.description: The person's CRM contact carries one of these tags (case-insensitive).

reached.description: The person reached one of these funnel steps, any source the brand connected (form submitted, appointment booked / showed / no-show, signup, website visit, sale).

notReached.description: The person reached none of these steps.

includeClients.description: Default false: people who reached `sale` (a deal won, a payment that stands) are out.

includeOptedOut.description: Default false: people the CRM marks do-not-contact are out.

allOf.description: A part of the brand's own CRM. Inside a list any one entry matches; across keys all must match. Clients and opted-out people are always out unless stated.
Only people in this part of the brand's own CRM (pipeline stage, tag, funnel step...). Scopes a CRM sourcing to a segment.

people.description: Serve from the brand's merged PEOPLE (one row per human, every source) instead of its CSV rows. Exclusive with uploadIds. Always excludes automated senders, people not about this brand, anyone without an email, and anyone the CRM marks do-not-contact (unless segment.includeOptedOut). Same brand-wide no-re-serve: every address of a served person is suppressed, and a person any address of whom was served before is never served.

reachableBy.description: The channel(s) the pipe serving writes on (all required): `phone` (WhatsApp, calls, SMS) or `email`. On BOTH pools, a contact or person the pipe cannot reach is SKIPPED and NOT marked served, so it stays available to a pipe that can. Omit = no requirement (unchanged behaviour).

relationships.description: The pipe's relationship policy (its lead strategy, forwarded by human-service). `business_only`: lead-service is asked who each candidate is to the brand (POST /internal/brands/{brandId}/relationships/query); nobody tagged personal, investor, supplier, team, partner or advisor (sure or unsure), nobody lead-service never judged, nobody without a human id is handed out, on BOTH pools. Such a person is NOT marked served (another pipe may still write to them). lead-service unreadable = 502 relationships_unavailable, nothing served. Omit = unchanged behaviour.

reached.description: The person reached one of these steps (any source the brand connected).

notReached.description: The person reached none of these steps.

allOf.description: The SERVING PIPE's funnel-step filter (stated by the play's workflow, forwarded by lead-service and human-service), cross-org words only: never a client's stage or tag name. ANDed with the pool and the audience's own filter, on BOTH pools (a CSV row is judged on the person holding its address). Clients are ALWAYS out when it is present. `sale` = a deal won, a payment that stands, or a CRM stage / tag Jev judged `client`; `disqualified` = a CRM stage / tag Jev judged `disqualified` (unqualified, bad fit, blocked: GET /orgs/gohighlevel/label-verdicts).
The serving pipe's funnel-step filter (see StepFilter). A person outside it is skipped and NOT marked served. Omit = unchanged behaviour.

includeEmailUnknown.description: CSV pool only (refused with people). After the sendable contacts, fill the rest of `limit` with contacts whose email is NOT known yet but that carry a name AND a company domain, company name or LinkedIn: returned in `contacts` with primaryEmail null, emailStatus unknown. Each is recorded handed out (never handed out twice; again after 24 h if nobody wrote back). The caller looks the email up and writes it back: POST /orgs/contacts/{contactId}/email-lookup. Same opt-out, consent, file, reach and step rules. Under relationships=business_only none is handed out (no known person to judge yet). Omit = unchanged behaviour.

200.description: Served contacts as returned by crm-service

post.summary: Merge two people into one person (they are the same human)
post.description:
Merge two people of a brand into ONE person when they are the same person on different channels and no source record says so (a WhatsApp chat with a number nobody saved, and the same human on Gmail or in the CRM). Proxy to crm-service POST /orgs/people/merges. Body `{ brandId, personIds: [personId, personId], reason? }` (the two personId values from GET /v1/orgs/people) forwarded verbatim. The two people become one merged thread with every channel and identity key of both; one person id is kept and the other still opens it. A rebuild starts at once: the merged person shows on GET /v1/orgs/people within about a minute. Idempotent: stating the same two people again answers 200 with `duplicate: true` (201 for a new merge). Refusals cross verbatim with their reason: 404 `person_not_found`, 422 `different_brand` / `same_person`, 409 `already_one_person`. Unmerge with POST /v1/orgs/people/merges/{mergeId}/undo. Requires x-user-id (recorded as who stated it). Response shape owned by crm-service.

Request body: documented from crm-service POST /orgs/people/merges, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.
