post.summary: Request a signup code by email (no API key needed)
post.description:
Step 1 of opening a distribute.you account as an AI agent, with no API key and no human. Sends a 6-digit code to `email`; read it in that inbox, then call POST /v1/agent-signups/complete. Works for an email that already has an account too (that is how you get another API key for it). Requesting a new code cancels the earlier ones. Answer (from client-service, verbatim): `{email, expiresAt, codeTtlMinutes, maxAttempts}`. Agent flow, no human needed except to pay: (1) POST /v1/agent-signups/start with your email + phone, (2) read the 6-digit code in that inbox, (3) POST /v1/agent-signups/complete with email + code → `apiKey`, (4) call any free endpoint with `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`, (5) before anything that spends money, POST /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_checkout and have the returned `url` paid. There is no free credit.

Response: documented from client-service POST /internal/agent-signups/start, which owns it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

expiresAt.description: ISO instant after which this code is refused (`code_expired`).

maxAttempts.description: Wrong guesses allowed on this code before it dies (`too_many_attempts`).

post.summary: Verify the code and get an API key (no API key needed)
post.description: Step 2: send the email and the 6-digit code; get back a working API key plus your org and user ids. A new email opens an account (organization + user; the email is the account's contact, the person can later sign in to the dashboard with it). An email that already has an account gets a NEW additional key for that same account (`created: false`): call start + complete again whenever you need another key. The account has NO free credit: free endpoints work at once, and anything that spends money answers 402 `payment_required` until you prepay (see `prepay` in the answer). A 429 with `error: "too_many_attempts"` means this code is burned after too many wrong tries: request a new one with POST /v1/agent-signups/start (any other 429 is the rate limit). Agent flow, no human needed except to pay: (1) POST /v1/agent-signups/start with your email + phone, (2) read the 6-digit code in that inbox, (3) POST /v1/agent-signups/complete with email + code → `apiKey`, (4) call any free endpoint with `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`, (5) before anything that spends money, POST /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_checkout and have the returned `url` paid. There is no free credit.

200.description: The account and a new API key

post.summary: Prepay: get a payment link (amount you choose, auto top-up required)
post.description:
Call this when a call answered 402 `payment_required`, or before anything that spends money. Returns `url`, a hosted card payment page charging `topup_amount_cents`. Paying it credits the balance with exactly that amount (no free credit is ever added), saves the card, and arms the MANDATORY automatic top-up: whenever the balance would fall below `auto_topup_threshold_cents`, the card is charged `auto_topup_amount_cents`. Minimums: $10 prepay, $15 reload, $5 threshold; below a minimum the answer is 400 `amount_below_minimum` naming the `field` and its `minimum_cents` (a missing or non-integer amount is 400 `invalid_amount`). No subscription on this path. You cannot pay the page yourself unless you hold a card: give `url` to your human. Then poll GET /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_status until `state` is `active`. Example: prepay $10 → balance $10; it drops under $5 → the card is charged $15. Answer from billing-service, verbatim: `{url, session_id, org_id, payment_mode: "prepaid", free_credit_offer, topup_amount_cents, auto_topup: {amount_cents, threshold_cents}}`.

Response: documented from billing-service POST /v1/accounts/prepaid_checkout, which owns it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

url.description: Hosted payment page. Paying it charges topup_amount_cents and saves the card for the automatic reloads.

get.summary: Prepaid status: paid yet? balance, auto top-up, can the card be reloaded?
get.description:
Read after giving a payment `url` to your human, and whenever a paid call is refused. `state`: `awaiting_payment` (nothing paid yet: the page has not been paid, open a new checkout if the link expired) | `active` (paid, auto top-up armed, card reloadable: you can spend) | `card_not_reloadable` (paid, but the card cannot be charged automatically, `card.not_reloadable_reason` says why: `no_saved_card`, `card_issuing_country_unsupported`, `prepaid_card`, `recurring_charge_not_authorized`, `card_unusable`; the balance is spendable but will not refill: ask your human to pay a new prepaid checkout with another card) | `auto_topup_off` (prepaid without reload: open a prepaid checkout to arm it) | `not_prepaid` (the org pays another way). Also `balance_cents`, `paid_cents`, `auto_topup {enabled, amount_cents, threshold_cents}`, `card {saved, reloadable, not_reloadable_reason}`. Answer from billing-service, verbatim; 404 = no billing account yet (nothing paid).

Response: documented from billing-service GET /v1/accounts/prepaid_status, which owns it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

state.description: `awaiting_payment` nothing paid and no card yet. `active` prepaid, auto top-up armed, the saved card can be reloaded. `card_not_reloadable` the payment landed (credit is spendable) but the card cannot be charged with nobody present: no reload will fire, add another card (POST /v1/accounts/card_setup). `auto_topup_off` prepaid without auto top-up. `not_prepaid` postpaid or subscription.

paid_cents.description: Money paid in, net of refunds (decimal cents).

get.summary: The API document for this key
get.description: The OpenAPI document of every operation THIS key may call. For a customer key it is the public document (`GET /openapi.json`). For a distribute.you staff member's key it also carries the staff operations a staff key may call, each under the `Staff (key)` tag. The distribute.you MCP reads it to know what a session can do. Revalidate instead of re-downloading: the response carries an `ETag`; send it back as `If-None-Match` and an unchanged document answers 304 with no body. Reads of this document are not recorded on your conversation thread.

post.summary: Reply to a person in their existing email thread
post.description:
Send an answer into the email thread a person already has with the brand, from the mailbox and persona that wrote to them (the reply a sales rep would send). Name the person by `email` alone: the thread is found from it. When that person wrote back on several campaigns the answer is 409 `ambiguous_thread` with the `candidates`; call again with one `campaign_id`. Write `body_html` without a signature (the persona's is added). Send `sent_by: "human"` for a reply a person decided on. Name the organization with `brandId` or `orgId`. To send files, list offer documents in `attachments` [{ document_id }] (up to 5, 10 MB together; ids from `GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers/{offerId}/documents`): each goes as a real email attachment, and any problem refuses the whole reply, nothing sent (404 `attachment_not_found`, 422 `attachment_too_large` or `attachments_unsupported_on_transport`, 502 `attachment_unavailable`). Pass-through to instantly-service POST /orgs/replies: refusals come back unchanged with a `code` (409 `ambiguous_thread`, `no_reply_to_thread`, `human_took_over`; 404 `campaign_not_found` when the org never emailed that person). The full body is documented from instantly-service.

Request body: documented from instantly-service POST /orgs/replies, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

campaign_id.description: Logical campaign id — the same key manual qualifications and opt-outs use. OPTIONAL: omit it and the thread is found from `email` alone. A thread is a campaign of this org in which the prospect wrote back. Exactly one → the reply goes into it. Several → 409 `ambiguous_thread` listing each candidate (`campaign_id` + `last_message_at`); call again naming one. None but we did email them → 409 `no_reply_to_thread`. Never emailed by this org → 404 `campaign_not_found`. When given, it is used as-is.

email.description: The prospect who replied. Matched case-insensitively. Enough on its own to find the thread when `campaign_id` is omitted.

body_html.description: The answer, HTML. Signed by this service with the sending account's persona — do NOT include a signature.

sent_by.description: Who asked for this answer to be sent. It decides ONE thing: whether the human-takeover gate applies. An `automation` reply is refused (409 `human_took_over`) once a person has answered the thread since the prospect last wrote and that answer is not yet counted as our touch; a `human` reply is never gated. Absent resolves to `automation` — the automated responder is the only caller today, so the gate is live without waiting on it, and a human surface declares `human` explicitly.

document_id.description: An offer document id (UUID) from brand-service, of THIS org (x-org-id).

attachments.description: Offer documents to attach to the reply as real files (a case study, a one-pager). This service reads each one from brand-service, bytes included, as this org, and attaches it under brand-service's filename and type. Up to 5, 10 MB together. FAIL LOUD, nothing sent: unknown or another org's document = 404 `attachment_not_found`; over the limits = 422 `attachment_too_large`; brand-service unreadable = 502 `attachment_unavailable`; a thread on the Instantly pipe (no attachment support) = 422 `attachments_unsupported_on_transport`. Absent or empty = the reply exactly as before. Replies only: cold sequence steps never carry a file.

post.summary: Invite a person to the organization by email
post.description:
Invite someone to join this organization: send their `email`. Returns the `invitation` with its `inviteUrl`, the link to forward by hand (they also get it by email). Inviting the same email again returns the pending invitation (200) instead of a second one. Any member of the organization may invite. The inviter is taken from the key. Pass-through to client-service POST /internal/orgs/{orgId}/member-invitations.

Open `linkUrl` (`https://t.me/<bot>?start=<code>`) and press Start in Telegram: that chat then gets the notices. Good once, for 30 minutes (`expiresAt`). Connecting again replaces the chat linked before. No body: the member connecting is taken from the key. Pass-through to client-service POST /internal/orgs/{orgId}/owner-telegram/link-codes.

get.summary: Review who each person is to a brand: unsure merges, unsure tags, unknown companies, and everything settled
get.description: What the brand's relationship review needs: `mergeQuestions` (two people the AI thinks may be the same person, each with a `confidence` and a `reason`), `tagQuestions` (a tag the AI is unsure about), `companyQuestions` (people whose company is unknown, with candidates), `settled` (merges done and every person with their company and tags) and `counts`. Fix each with the POST/PUT/DELETE routes under the same path. Tags: `personal` (about the PERSON, shown on every brand) and `customer`, `prospect`, `team`, `investor`, `advisor`, `supplier`, `partner`, `other_professional` (about this person at this brand). Undo a merge with POST .../relationships/merges/{linkId}/undo. Pass-through to lead-service POST /orgs/brands/{brandId}/relationships/merge-questions/{questionId}/answer.
